# Templates are re-parsed to locate their actions, and that re-parse has to
# go through text/template rather than through text/template/parse.
#
# text/template defines the builtins -- eq, and, index, len and the rest --
# and passes them to the parser. The parse package on its own rejects a
# call to any function it was not handed, so parsing there directly makes
# every template using a builtin fail to enumerate.
#
# TestStatus only renders a code of 200, so forcing the condition true
# changes nothing it sees and that mutant survives. Forcing it false swaps
# the branch and is caught.

muxt test-template-mutations
cmp stdout want.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "status"}}{{if eq .Code 200}}ok{{else}}bad{{end}}{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Status struct {
	Code int
}

func Render(w io.Writer, status Status) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "status", status)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestStatus(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Status{Code: 200}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "ok"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("status = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
